cards.explanation: The answer is to test him with hard questions. The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and came "…to test him with difficult questions." (2 Chronicles 9:1). Solomon was the one with the reputation, and she wanted to see if it held up. I would have brought a pop quiz and a box of cookies, but she brought a whole caravan.

The answer is False. The Bible says "…Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain." (2 Chronicles 9:2). She came ready with difficult questions about all that was on her mind. Every one of them got an answer. I get stumped by a stuck cookie lid, so this impresses me, friends.

The answer is breath. After she saw Solomon's wisdom, the palace, the food at his table, his servants and the burnt offerings at the house of the LORD, "…it took her breath away." (2 Chronicles 9:4). That's a whole lot of looking. I think she needed a minute to sit down.

The answer is False. The queen says it herself: "…I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes." (2 Chronicles 9:6). She heard the stories, and then she packed up a caravan to check. That's a long trip to double-check a rumor, and I respect it.

The answer is that he far exceeds them. She says, "…not half of the greatness of your wisdom was told to me. You have far exceeded the report I heard." (2 Chronicles 9:6). The reports were big, and the real thing was bigger. That's hard to pull off when the hype is already loud, friends.

The answer is the LORD. The queen says, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on His throne…" (2 Chronicles 9:8). She had just praised Solomon's servants, and then she turned to the LORD. It's the LORD she calls blessed.

The answer is justice. The queen says that because God loved Israel enough to establish them forever, He made Solomon king "…to carry out justice and righteousness." (2 Chronicles 9:8). That's what she says the kingship was for. And she said it standing in front of him.

The answer is True! The text says, "There had never been such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon." (2 Chronicles 9:9). She brought gold and precious stones too, but the spices get the special mention. Those camels were carrying the good stuff, friends.

The answer is the singers. Solomon made the algum wood into "…lyres and harps for the singers." (2 Chronicles 9:11). The same wood also became steps for the house of the LORD and for the king's palace. And nothing like it had been seen in Judah before.

The answer is False. Solomon gave the queen "…all she desired—whatever she asked—far more than she had brought the king." (2 Chronicles 9:12). That's after she showed up with a caravan of gold, spices and precious stones. I'd have to bake a lot of cookies to try to match that, friends.
